provenance: Editorial TOPIK II Level 5 formal/advanced grammar selection, not an official exam checklist; educator review required.

grammarPoints.title: N(으)로 인해(서)
grammarPoints.hint: State a cause or source of change in formal news, reports or explanatory writing.
grammarPoints.description: State a cause or source of change in formal news, reports or explanatory writing. It is a formal way of identifying the cause of an event or change.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Put (으)로 인해(서) after a noun denoting the cause: 사고로 인해, 폭우로 인해서.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 폭우로 인해 비행기가 취소됐어요. — The flight was cancelled due to heavy rain. 폭우로 인해 presents heavy rain as the formal cause of a cancelled flight.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is more formal than 때문에; do not attach the particle directly to a bare verb stem.

lessonExamples.englishHint: The flight was cancelled due to heavy rain.
Traffic was blocked because of an accident.

cards.englishHint: Life changed due to technological progress.
The road was closed because of construction.
The event was delayed due to an infection outbreak.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㅁ으로써
grammarPoints.hint: Show the means or method by which a result is achieved, often in formal writing.
grammarPoints.description: Use -(으)ㅁ으로써 to explain the action or method by which a result is achieved in formal writing. The verb takes nominalizing -(으)ㅁ before 으로써; its shape changes with the stem ending.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Form a noun from an action verb: 하다 → 함으로써, 보다 → 봄으로써, 읽다 → 읽음으로써. This is a method, not the role marker -(으)로서.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 반복함으로써 실력이 늘었어요. — My skill improved through repetition. Compare 읽음으로써 (consonant stem) with 봄으로써 (vowel stem).

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Do not confuse -으로써 (by means of) with -으로서 (in the role of).

lessonExamples.englishHint: My skill improved through repetition.
Reading books broadened my perspective.

cards.englishHint: I gained experience by participating.
I gained new ideas by reading books.
I understood the difference by seeing it firsthand.

grammarPoints.title: N에 따라(서)
grammarPoints.hint: Express variation by a factor, or following a rule or standard.
grammarPoints.description: N에 따라(서) has two related but distinct uses: outcomes vary depending on a factor (사람에 따라 다르다), or actions are carried out according to a rule or standard (규정에 따라 처리하다). Both 에 따라 and 에 따라서 fit the lesson's examples.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 에 따라 or 에 따라서 to a noun: 날씨에 따라 일정이 바뀌어요 (depending on weather); 규정에 따라서 처리하세요 (according to regulations).

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 상황에 따라 계획이 달라져요. — Plans change depending on the situation. 규정에 따라서 신청서를 제출하세요 means following an established rule, not varying with the rule.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Don't treat every 에 따라 as a direct cause like 때문에. A variation context asks what differs; a standard-following context asks which rule governs the action.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Plans change depending on the situation.
Submit the application according to the rules.

cards.englishHint: Opinions differ from person to person. (Indicate variation by a factor or following a stated standard.)
Please handle it according to the rules. (Indicate variation by a factor or following a stated standard.)

cards.fullSentence: 날씨에 따라 일정이 바뀔 수 있어요.
cards.englishHint: The schedule may change depending on weather. (Indicate variation by a factor or following a stated standard.)

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 바
grammarPoints.hint: Refer formally to what is known, stated or observed, often in official writing.
grammarPoints.description: Refer formally to what is known, stated or observed, often in official writing. It refers to something stated, known or observed in formal writing.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 바 after a present action or -(으)ㄴ 바 after a completed action.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 제가 확인한 바에 따르면 문제가 없어요. — According to what I confirmed, there's no issue. 확인한 바에 따르면 points back to findings already established.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: 바 is a bound noun and must be separated; this formal sense is not ordinary 장소 ('place').

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 제가 확인한 바에 따르면 문제가 없어요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: According to what I confirmed, there's no issue.
Proceed as explained above.

cards.englishHint: According to reports, there was a change.
I organized what I investigated.
Contrary to what was known, the result differed.

lessons.title: Degree, tendency and only one outcome

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 만큼
grammarPoints.hint: Express a matching degree: 'as much as', 'in proportion to', or 'given that'.
grammarPoints.description: Express a matching degree: 'as much as', 'in proportion to', or 'given that'. It compares the degree of one thing with another or gives the corresponding extent.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 만큼 after actions, -(으)ㄴ 만큼 after descriptions or completed actions.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 노력한 만큼 성과가 나와요. — You get results in proportion to your effort. 노력한 만큼 says the reward corresponds to the amount of effort.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is not always a plain comparison of two sizes; context can imply a justified expectation.

lessonExamples.englishHint: You get results in proportion to your effort.
Your skill grows as much as you practice.

cards.englishHint: It was as good as I had expected.
I learned in proportion to the time spent.
Because it's so important, we must be careful.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 법이다
grammarPoints.hint: Express a general rule about how things usually happen: 'it's the nature of things'.
grammarPoints.description: Express a general rule about how things usually happen: 'it's the nature of things'. It states that a behavior or outcome is natural or generally expected.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 법이다 after an action verb or -(으)ㄴ 법이다 after some descriptive predicates.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 누구나 실수하는 법이에요. — Everyone makes mistakes; it's natural. 실수하는 법이에요 presents mistakes as a normal part of learning.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This claims a general tendency, not a legal rule or a prediction of one specific event.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Everyone makes mistakes; it's natural.
Things naturally fade with time.

cards.englishHint: It's natural for things to be hard at first.

cards.fullSentence: 열심히 하면 늘기 마련이지만 실수도 하는 법이에요.
cards.englishHint: Improvement is natural, but so are mistakes.
People naturally change.

grammarPoints.title: -게 마련이다
grammarPoints.hint: Say a result is natural, expected or nearly inevitable.
grammarPoints.description: Say a result is natural, expected or nearly inevitable. It expresses that a result is only to be expected.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 게 마련이다 to a verb or descriptive stem: 변하다 → 변하게 마련이다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 시간이 지나면 변하게 마련이에요. — Things are bound to change with time. 시간이 지나면 변하게 마련이에요 treats change as a natural expectation.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This describes a tendency, not an absolute mathematical law; do not use for every casual prediction.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Things are bound to change with time.
You're bound to make mistakes at first.

cards.englishHint: With effort, skill naturally improves.
Everyone inevitably grows old.
New things are naturally difficult.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 따름이다
grammarPoints.hint: Emphasize that a feeling, motive or action is simply all there is: 'only / merely'.
grammarPoints.description: Emphasize that a feeling, motive or action is simply all there is: 'only / merely'. It restricts the speaker's statement to a single feeling or conclusion.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)ㄹ to a predicate stem, then 따름이에요; often used with emotions or modest explanations.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 도와주셔서 감사할 따름이에요. — All I can say is that I'm grateful. 감사할 따름이에요 says the speaker can do nothing but feel thankful.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is a formal or literary limitation, not the everyday restriction particle 만.

lessonExamples.englishHint: All I can say is that I'm grateful.
All we can do is wait for the result.

cards.englishHint: I can only do my best.
I'm simply amazed.
I'm simply delighted by the news.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ지라도
grammarPoints.hint: Concede even a strong hypothetical condition: 'even if / even though'.
grammarPoints.description: Concede even a strong hypothetical condition: 'even if / even though'. It allows a contrary condition while asserting the final outcome.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)ㄹ지라도 to the predicate stem before the outcome that still holds.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 어려울지라도 끝까지 하겠습니다. — Even if it is difficult, I will finish. 어렵더라도 is common, while 어려울지라도 gives the concession more written emphasis.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is often formal and emphatic; do not overuse it in casual chat.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Even if it is difficult, I will finish.
Even if I fail, I won't regret it.

cards.englishHint: Even if it rains, we will depart.
Even if it takes time, I will wait.
Even if small, it has meaning.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ망정
grammarPoints.hint: Accept one unfavorable possibility while rejecting a worse choice: 'even if..., at least...'.
grammarPoints.description: Accept one unfavorable possibility while rejecting a worse choice: 'even if..., at least...'. It asserts that a speaker accepts a cost but still maintains their choice.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -(으)ㄹ망정 after a stem, typically followed by a strong contrasting choice.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 굶을망정 거짓말은 안 해요. — I'd rather go hungry than lie. 굶을망정 거짓말은 안 해요 means I would rather go hungry than lie.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: It has a dramatic, emphatic tone; ordinary -지만 is not a direct substitute.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I'd rather go hungry than lie.
Even if I fail, I won't give up.

cards.englishHint: Even at a loss, I'll keep my promise.
Even if scolded, I'll tell the truth.
Even if I'm late, I won't rush.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ들
grammarPoints.hint: Rhetorically concede an imagined condition: 'even if that were the case, what difference?'.
grammarPoints.description: Rhetorically concede an imagined condition: 'even if that were the case, what difference?'. It asks rhetorically whether a hypothetical difference would matter.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach -(으)ㄴ들 to a verb or description; the next clause often questions its value.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 돈이 많은들 행복할까요? — Even with lots of money, would you be happy? 돈이 많은들 행복할까요? asks whether wealth alone would ensure happiness.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is elevated rhetorical grammar, not an everyday conditional like -(으)면.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Even with lots of money, would you be happy?
Even if you regret it now, nothing changes.

cards.englishHint: Even if you try alone, it isn't enough.
Even if you talk a lot, it's useless.
However busy you are, you need sleep.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 바에야
grammarPoints.hint: Prefer an alternative rather than accept an undesirable situation: 'if I must..., I'd rather...'.
grammarPoints.description: Prefer an alternative rather than accept an undesirable situation: 'if I must..., I'd rather...'. It evaluates the proposed action as worse than choosing another alternative.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -(으)ㄹ 바에야 after the rejected action, then give the preferred action.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 기다릴 바에야 걸어가겠어요. — I'd rather walk than wait. 기다릴 바에야 걸어가겠어요 presents walking as preferable to waiting.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: The structure highlights the rejected option; do not confuse it with plain future -ㄹ 거예요.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I'd rather walk than wait.
I'd rather try again than give up.

cards.englishHint: I'd rather stay silent than lie.
I'd rather try than regret it.
I'd rather go tomorrow than arrive late.

grammarPoints.title: -기는커녕
grammarPoints.hint: Emphatically deny even an expected minimum: 'far from doing X, Y'.
grammarPoints.description: Emphatically deny even an expected minimum: 'far from doing X, Y'. It strongly rejects the very possibility mentioned, often 'let alone'.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기는커녕 to an action stem; the next clause presents an even less favorable reality.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 쉬기는커녕 밤새 일했어요. — Far from resting, I worked all night. 쉬기는커녕 밤새 일했어요: not only did the speaker not rest, they worked all night.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is strong rhetorical contrast, not a neutral noun choice or mild -지만.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Far from resting, I worked all night.
Instead of praise, I got scolded.

cards.englishHint: Far from winning, we didn't score.
I couldn't even drink water, let alone eat.
Instead of helping, they got in the way.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄹ 겨를이 없다
grammarPoints.hint: Have no spare time or mental room to do something.
grammarPoints.description: Have no spare time or mental room to do something. It states that someone has no time or opportunity even to start an action.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Put -(으)ㄹ before the bound noun 겨를, followed by 이 없어요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 밥을 먹을 겨를이 없어요. — I don't have a moment to eat. 밥을 먹을 겨를이 없어요 means being too busy even to eat.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is stronger and more idiomatic than just saying 시간이 없어요.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I don't have a moment to eat.
There was no time to rest.

cards.englishHint: I didn't even have time to think. (Express lacking even the time or chance to attempt this.)
I had no time to say hello. (Express lacking even the time or chance to attempt this.)
I have no chance to look around. (Express lacking even the time or chance to attempt this.)

grammarPoints.title: -기가 무섭게
grammarPoints.hint: One event happens immediately upon another, with a vivid sense of speed.
grammarPoints.description: One event happens immediately upon another, with a vivid sense of speed. It stresses how immediately a second event follows the first.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 기가 무섭게 to the first action stem, then describe what came immediately next.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 문을 열기가 무섭게 고양이가 뛰어나갔어요. — The cat dashed out the instant the door opened. 문을 열기가 무섭게 means the next action occurred virtually the instant the door opened.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is more dramatic than -자마자; it is a time connector, not literal fear.

lessonExamples.englishHint: The cat dashed out the instant the door opened.
They left as soon as class ended.

cards.englishHint: I fell asleep the instant I got home.
I contacted them as soon as I heard.
I picked up the instant it rang.

grammarPoints.title: N조차
grammarPoints.hint: Even the least expected person or thing is included or excluded: 'even'.
grammarPoints.description: Even the least expected person or thing is included or excluded: 'even'. It emphasizes that even the named item falls within an unexpected range.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 조차 directly to a noun or noun phrase: 이름조차, 친구조차.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 그 사람의 이름조차 몰라요. — I don't even know that person's name. 이름조차 몰라요 stresses that the speaker does not know even the name.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: 조차 often appears with negative or surprising statements; it is more emphatic than 도.

lessonExamples.englishHint: I don't even know that person's name.
Even my friends didn't believe me.

cards.englishHint: I didn't even know the basic rules.
I couldn't even drink a glass of water.
I couldn't hear even the slightest sound.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 데 비해
grammarPoints.hint: Contrast one situation against another using a measured comparison.
grammarPoints.description: Contrast one situation against another using a measured comparison. It contrasts two situations using a clear comparison standard.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -는 데 비해 after an action or -(으)ㄴ 데 비해 after a description.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 가격이 비싼 데 비해 품질이 좋아요. — Compared with its high price, the quality is good. 가격이 비싼 데 비해 품질이 좋아요 compares cost with quality.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is analytical comparison; don't confuse the bound noun 데 with a physical location.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 가격이 비싼 데 비해 품질이 좋아요.
lessonExamples.englishHint: Compared with its high price, the quality is good.
The result is small compared with the effort.

cards.englishHint: It was easier than I expected.

cards.fullSentence: 시간이 걸린 데 비해 결과가 좋아요.
cards.englishHint: The outcome is good given the time spent.

cards.fullSentence: 형은 조용한 데 비해 동생은 활발해요.
cards.englishHint: The older brother is quiet, while the younger is lively.

grammarPoints.title: -는 대로 (immediately)
grammarPoints.hint: Act as soon as a first event happens, with little or no intervening delay.
grammarPoints.description: Act as soon as a first event happens, with little or no intervening delay. It presents the next event as following immediately when the first is done.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 는 대로 to the first action verb stem, followed by the action to do at once.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 도착하는 대로 전화하세요. — Call me as soon as you arrive. 도착하는 대로 전화하세요 means to call immediately upon arriving.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: -는 대로 can also mean 'as/according to' in other contexts; here it marks prompt sequence.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Call me as soon as you arrive.
I'll leave as soon as work ends.

cards.englishHint: Let me know as soon as the result comes out.
We'll start as soon as things are ready.
I'll contact you whenever I find time.

grammarPoints.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 바와 같이
grammarPoints.hint: Refer back formally to something stated or observed: 'as explained / as shown'.
grammarPoints.description: Refer back formally to something stated or observed: 'as explained / as shown'. It formally refers to what was just said or demonstrated.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use -(으)ㄴ/는 바와 같이 after an event or statement being cited.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 보고서에 적힌 바와 같이 진행하세요. — Proceed as written in the report. 적힌 바와 같이 refers to instructions already written in the report.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is formal and refers to established information; it isn't everyday -처럼 comparison.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Proceed as written in the report.
As stated earlier, it has changed.

cards.fullSentence: 조사에서 확인된 바와 같이 차이가 있어요.
cards.englishHint: As confirmed by the study, there is a difference.
The result was as expected.

cards.fullSentence: 앞서 언급한 바와 같이 주의가 필요해요.
cards.englishHint: As mentioned earlier, caution is needed.

grammarPoints.title: N에 불과하다
grammarPoints.hint: Describe something as only a small or limited amount/status: 'no more than'.
grammarPoints.description: Describe something as only a small or limited amount/status: 'no more than'. It states that the amount or situation is no more than a limited figure.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Put 에 불과하다 after a noun or quantity and conjugate 불과하다: 숫자에 불과해요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 그것은 추측에 불과해요. — That's nothing more than speculation. 예상은 추측에 불과해요 dismisses a prediction as mere speculation.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: This is evaluative limitation, stronger than neutral N만; it can sound dismissive.

lessonExamples.englishHint: That's nothing more than speculation.
The current figure is only an estimate.

cards.englishHint: He's only a student.
This result is only the beginning.
That was just a minor mistake. (Downplay the thing as only the stated amount or status.)

grammarPoints.title: -고자 하다
grammarPoints.hint: Express an intention or purpose in formal writing, presentations or announcements.
grammarPoints.description: Express an intention or purpose in formal writing, presentations or announcements. It expresses formal, deliberate intention, common in proposals and writing.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 고자 하다 to an action stem: 설명하다 → 설명하고자 합니다.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 오늘 결과를 설명하고자 합니다. — Today I intend to explain the results. 설명하고자 합니다 frames explaining as the formal purpose of the speaker.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: It is formal, not a default casual substitute for -려고 하다.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Today I intend to explain the results.
I wish to propose a new method.

cards.englishHint: We would like to hear opinions. (Express formal intention in written or public speech.)
We tried to solve the problem.
I wrote to announce the change.

grammarPoints.title: -고 말다
grammarPoints.hint: An action ends up happening decisively, often despite attempts to prevent it.
grammarPoints.description: An action ends up happening decisively, often despite attempts to prevent it. It stresses that an action finally happened, often against the speaker's preference.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Attach 고 말다 to the action stem; the common past is -고 말았어요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 결국 울고 말았어요. — In the end, I burst into tears. 울고 말았어요 emphasizes that the speaker ultimately ended up crying.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: The feeling may be regret, frustration or determination; it isn't simply a neutral sequence with -고.

lessonExamples.englishHint: In the end, I burst into tears.
I ended up revealing the secret.

cards.englishHint: I couldn't help laughing in the end. (Describe an eventual and often unwelcome outcome.)
I ended up deleting the file by mistake. (Describe an eventual and often unwelcome outcome.)
I ended up breaking my promise. (Describe an eventual and often unwelcome outcome.)

grammarPoints.title: -아/어도 소용없다
grammarPoints.hint: Even if someone tries something, it will not help or change the outcome.
grammarPoints.description: Even if someone tries something, it will not help or change the outcome. It says that even trying will not make a meaningful difference.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Use the verb's 아/어도 form before 소용없어요: 기다리다 → 기다려도 소용없어요.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 지금 서둘러도 소용없어요. — Hurrying now won't help. 지금 서둘러도 소용없어요 says hurrying now cannot undo the delay.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Similar to -아/어 봤자, but this construction explicitly states the lack of usefulness.

lessonExamples.englishHint: Hurrying now won't help.
Asking again won't help.

cards.englishHint: Regretting it is pointless. (Concede the action but show it would be futile.)
Worrying alone won't help. (Concede the action but show it would be futile.)
Waiting longer won't help. (Concede the action but show it would be futile.)

grammarPoints.title: -기 십상이다
grammarPoints.hint: Say an undesirable result is very likely given the circumstances.
grammarPoints.description: Say an undesirable result is very likely given the circumstances. It warns that an unfavorable outcome is quite likely.

notes.title: Build it step by step
notes.content: Add 기 십상이다 to an action stem, often in formal or cautionary statements.

notes.title: Worked example
notes.content: 서두르면 실수하기 십상이에요. — If you rush, you're likely to make mistakes. 서두르면 실수하기 십상이에요 says rushing often leads to mistakes.

notes.title: Common trap
notes.content: Unlike neutral -기 쉽다, this phrase often points to an unwelcome result.

lessonExamples.englishHint: If you rush, you're likely to make mistakes.

lessonExamples.fullSentence: 관리를 안 하면 고장 나기 십상이에요.
